To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
- Charmonium production at low energies is sensitive to nuclear substructure, and can identify hot spots of high density in nuclei.

the color singlet model fails in describing high energy photo and hadroproduction, that color evaporation models have problems in explaining the nuclear target dependence and the polarization in high energy photo and pion production, and that the color octet model has problems in describing high energy pion production.

charmonium photoproduction at 30 GeV electron energies is a promising probe of nuclear target structure, that charmonium photo- and hadronproduction at threshold energies will allow to study c cbar bound states in nuclear matter and that the production of charmonium in e +e - collisions is a good probe of color dynamics in QCD.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of heavy quark production in electron-nucleon scattering at energies of 15... 40 GeV. We are particularly interested in the production of charmed quarkonia, which is sensitive to the color structure of the interaction, and to the structure of the nucleon.
the production of heavy quarkonium in high energy collisions.

the following issues: 1) the determination of c c bar production mechanisms and the extraction of the c cbar interaction in nuclear matter, 2) the study of charmonium production on nuclei, and 3) the study of the target structure at the level of the nuclear substructure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
charmonium is an ideal probe of color dynamics and nuclear structure.
charmonium photoproduction is a sensitive tool for probing the structure of the target and the dynamics of the QCD interaction.
charmonium physics is very rich in its potential for new discoveries and tests of QCD, but that it is also a very difficult field, requiring a large variety of experimental approaches.

we have shown that the color evaporation model can explain the charmonium production cross-section data, but only if the model parameters are chosen in such a way that the model is not in agreement with other charmonium data.

a continuous electron beam facility with energies in the 15... 50 GeV range will be able to address a broad range of charmonium production issues.
